conviction_note: Balanced evidence: the one counterparty that spoke after Marsh's July call (Gallagher, 23 Sep) held Q3 brokerage organic at ~5% and reported US property renewal premiums falling less (-7% Jul-Aug vs -12% in Q2), and Accenture's consulting quarter was firm. Against that, Marsh's own Q2 rate index (-6%, steeper than Q1's -5%), mid-year reinsurance cat rates (-16%), moderating Ivans small-commercial renewals and a guide that puts more margin expansion in Q4 than Q3. The findings sum to +0.20, the scaled number is +0.08 (p_up 51 x abs 4.2). They agree in sign and both are close to a non-result. The name's reactions are fat-tailed (-8.5% on a 4% organic print in Oct 2025, -0.3% on a 5% organic beat in Jul 2026), so abs_move stays near the historical median even though direction is a coin flip.
bar: Adjusted EPS $1.96-$1.97 on revenue $6.63-6.65bn. Two sources agree: Benzinga $1.97 / $6.65B (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MRSH/earnings-forecasts) and Earnings Whispers $1.96 / $6.63B (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/MRSH). Metirai has $1.96 on 10 estimates, range $1.92-$2.00 (https://www.metirai.com/finance/MRSH/earnings). Year-ago adj EPS was $1.85 and underlying growth 4% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/62709/000006270925000123/mmc3q2025ex991newsrelease.htm). The company guide, from the Q2 call on 2026-07-21 (https://www.webull.com/news/15265646608851968): FY2026 underlying growth similar to 2025 (~4%); consulting Q3 mid-to-high single digits; fiduciary income ~$95m; corporate expense ~$75m; interest expense ~$250m; more margin expansion in Q4 than Q3; tax 24.5-25.5%. No sourced street estimate for Q3 organic growth exists, so organic-specific findings are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is 6,348,883 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, ~1.3% of shares outstanding, 1.87 days to cover (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/mrsh/short-interest, via the sweep row, read 2026-10-14). Not crowded. There is no usable skew: the front-expiry chain is unusable (ATM spread 156% of mid) and skew_25d is null. Put/call OI is 1.12 on 8,750 contracts. Tape: spot $177.13, 20d run-up +0.21%, 5d +2.0%, 14.4% below the 52-week high and 12.6% above the low, 20-day realised vol 14%. The CEO sold on 2026-09-02 at $188.51, so the stock is ~6% lower since early September. Unusual Whales says it is -5.7% since the last print. Headlines dated 2026-10-01 report BMO cutting its target to $179 from $203 and Goldman trimming to $191; these are headline-only and not verified.

findings.finding: Gallagher, the only large broker to speak on Q3 after Marsh's 21 July call, said on 23 Sep 2026 that Q3 brokerage organic growth is still about 5% with no change from earlier expectations. Its US retail property renewal premiums fell about 7% in July-August against about 12% in Q2. Casualty rose 7% and ex-property renewals were up about 4%, the same as Q2. A peer saw no further deceleration in Q3, and the property drag that weighs on Marsh's large-account, property-heavy book eased.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Organic growth is the line this name trades on. Oct 2025: 4% underlying with US/Canada at 3%, -8.52%. Apr 2026: 4% underlying beat, +4.39%. Jul 2026: 5% underlying beat (Marsh Risk 4%), -0.28% (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: It was public on 23 Sep, but on a peer's mid-quarter webcast that the wires rarely transcribe into Marsh numbers. Marsh fell ~6% from early September with targets being cut into the print. If the market had read the AJG data as a sign that broker organic growth is holding, MRSH would not be trading 14% off its high with a flat 20-day run-up.
findings.independence: Quartr's automated summary of the same Gallagher event repeats the -7% vs -12% property figure (https://quartr.com/events/arthur-j-gallagher-co-ajg-investor-update_3sBEWq0S); it is the same document, so not independent. WTW's Q2 CLIPS shows aggregate US pricing at +0.5% and large accounts negative (https://www.insurancejournal.com/magazines/mag-features/2026/10/05/887583.htm), which points the other way.

findings.finding: Marsh's own Global Insurance Market Index for Q2 2026 (published 23 Jul, two days after the Q2 call) shows global commercial rates down 6% after -5% in Q1 and -4% in Q3 2025. Property was -12%, casualty +2%, US +1%, and every region except the US fell. This is the eighth straight quarterly decline and it is steepening. The Q3 2026 reading (not yet published) is the rate backdrop for Marsh Risk commissions in the quarter being reported.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 rates fell 6% and Marsh Risk still grew 4% underlying (5% consolidated). The stock was -0.28%, so weak transmission from rates to organic growth. In Oct 2025 a 4% print against softer rates was sold -8.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is the company's own public index and the soft market is the consensus bear case. What may not be priced is that the decline accelerated after the Q2 call, while the FY guide ('similar to 2025') was given before it. A fully priced reading would show estimates cut, which the PT cuts suggest has partly happened.
findings.independence: CIAB Q2 2026: average premiums -2%, property -6.3%, large accounts -3.7% (https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2026/08/20/882240.htm). This is a different source pointing the same way, but it is also Q2 data.

findings.finding: Mid-year property-cat reinsurance rates-on-line fell 16% globally (-12% at 1 Jan), the steepest US annual decline since 2014, per Guy Carpenter's own 1 July report. Guy Carpenter revenue already fell 2% underlying in Q2 against +5% in Q3 2025. Q3 is a small GC quarter (H2 is about a quarter of its annual revenue, per the CFO), roughly 6% of group revenue, so the drag on the consolidated print is limited.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GC was -2% in Q2 2026 and the stock was -0.28%. The consulting beat offset it.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced; the GC softness was explicit on the Q2 call. The residual risk is Q3 commentary on Jan 1, 2027 renewals after a quiet hurricane season (forecasts below average, https://www.americanbanker.com/news/el-nino-means-less-active-atlantic-hurricane-season-in-2026). Net of the rest of the company, the impact is small.
findings.independence: JP Morgan sees no near-term floor in reinsurance rates (https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/reinsurance/news/breaking-news/jp-morgan-sees-no-nearterm-floor-as-reinsurance-rates-fall-16-at-midyear-581535.aspx).

findings.finding: Accenture's quarter to 31 Aug 2026 (reported 1 Oct) had consulting revenue of $9.28bn, +6% in USD. Total revenue of $18.7bn beat its guided $17.75-18.40bn, with book-to-bill 1.2. This is a consulting-demand read for Marsh Management Consulting (Oliver Wyman), which management guided to mid-to-high single digit underlying growth in Q3 after 13% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Consulting carried the Q2 2026 beat (+13%) and the stock was -0.28%, so consulting strength has not been paid much.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a cross-industry proxy (IT services, not strategy consulting) that sell-side broker models do not usually update on. If it were priced, consulting estimates would sit at the top of the guided range, and the preview language still frames consulting as decelerating.
findings.independence: None from a different source. This is a proxy, and Oliver Wyman's mix (financial services strategy) differs from Accenture's.

findings.finding: Insurance Business (25 Sep 2026) reports that Marsh is covered by IAG's confidential settlement of Credit Suisse's ~A$2.8bn Greensill claims, after the September trial was called off. Marsh booked a $425m provisional liability in Q1 2026 and has filed no 8-K since 21 July (EDGAR). The Q3 release is the first place the company can say whether the provision covers the deal; the item sits in noteworthy items, below adjusted operating income.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print carried the $425m charge and the stock rose 4.39%. The adjusted line drove the reaction and the charge did not.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a single trade-press source with confidential terms and no company statement. No 8-K suggests the result is not material relative to the provision. Removing a trial overhang is a small multiple positive; an extra charge would be excluded from adjusted EPS.
findings.independence: The EDGAR 8-K list shows no filing after 2026-07-21 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000062709&type=8-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=20), which is consistent with no material surprise. Q1 charge context: https://www.gtreview.com/news/global/marsh-books-us425mn-charge-ahead-of-greensill-trial/

findings.finding: CEO John Doyle exercised options (strike $73.195) and sold 16,656 shares at $188.51 on 2026-09-02, leaving 116,811 shares. The General Counsel did the same with 1,197 shares at $187.90 the same day. These are routine exercise-and-sell transactions of modest size, six weeks before the print and inside the window that follows the Q2 release.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 4s are public; this is weak information because it is an option exercise, not an open-market sale of held stock. It is filed for completeness.
findings.independence: GC Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/62709/000006270926000229/form4.xml. It is the same day and the same pattern, so not independent evidence.

findings.finding: The Ivans Index (small and middle-market commercial renewals, the Marsh Agency/MMA segment) decelerated in every main line from July to August 2026: property +5.69% vs +6.16%, GL +4.18% vs +4.99%, BOP +5.44% vs +5.94%, auto +3.58% vs +4.03%, umbrella +6.82% vs +7.42%. This is a mild headwind to rate-driven commission growth in Marsh's middle-market book.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific; middle-market has been the steadier part of US/Canada growth.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy: renewals are still positive in absolute terms and the change month to month is small. It is filed small because it is macro-to-company transmission that Marsh has not confirmed.
findings.independence: Gallagher's ex-property renewals were up ~4% in Jul-Aug, consistent with Q2 (finding 1). That source says flat, not down, so it partly contradicts this one.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call Marsh guided 'more margin expansion in the fourth quarter than in the third'. Q2 adjusted operating margin was 29.3% against 29.5% a year earlier, a 20bp contraction, despite Thrive savings ($239m of the ~$500m charges taken toward $400m of savings). The guide implies only modest Q3 margin expansion, and another flat or down margin would be a second quarter of no operating leverage.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul 2026: EPS and organic beat with margin down 20bp, stock -0.28%. A damped reaction to a beat with margin slippage.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits inside what the company guided, so the market was told to expect a small Q3 expansion. The finding stays small and is filed because margin was the line the July beat was not paid on.
findings.independence: The guidance quote is in the call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15265646608851968), which is the same event.

findings.finding: Q3 2025 is an easy comparison for the largest line. Marsh US/Canada grew only 3% underlying in Q3 2025 (consolidated 4%, RIS 3%), against 4% in Q2 2026. Guy Carpenter's comparison is tough (+5%), and consulting's (+5%) is moderate against a mid-to-high single digit guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The weak Q3 2025 US/Canada print is the one the stock fell 8.52% on, so the bar it set is low.
findings.why_not_priced: Comparisons are modelled, so this is mostly priced. It is filed because the consolidated revenue consensus (+4.3-4.7% reported with ~1pt from acquisitions) implies only ~3.5-4% underlying, which a 4%+ quarter on an easy US comparison would clear.
findings.independence: Barchart says the market expects +4.3% revenue growth (via the search result for https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3381048/marsh-nysemrsh-exceeds-q2-cy2026-expectations). It is a different source for the bar, not for the comparison.

findings.finding: Into the print, the stock has fallen from ~$188.5 (CEO Form 4 price, 2 Sep) to $177.13 (-6%), is 14.4% below its 52-week high and is -5.7% since the July print. Headlines on 1 Oct report BMO cutting its target to $179 and Goldman to $191, while JPMorgan raised to $215. Sentiment into the print is cautious, which lowers the bar for a reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Apr 2026 came into a down tape and rose +4.39% on an in-line-to-better quarter. Oct 2025 came in at highs and fell -8.52%.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is the price itself, so this is positioning, not information. Short interest is low (1.3%), so there is no squeeze mechanism. It is small and rests on headline-only target changes.

outside_window.finding: Jan 1, 2027 reinsurance renewals: after a below-average hurricane season and -16% mid-year cat rates, Guy Carpenter's 2027 revenue faces further rate pressure. The renewals themselves are dated after the window, though Q3 call commentary may preview them.

baseline_tension: No skew is available to agree with or contradict. The 20-day run-up is flat, while the stock sits ~6% below early-September levels and 14% off its high with targets cut, so the cautious positioning mildly favours a positive reaction to an in-line print. The fundamental evidence is balanced, so the call stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 9 (segment net of rest): Guy Carpenter finding cut from -0.3 to -0.15, since Q3 GC is ~6% of group revenue
Rule 5 (proxy vs company number): Marsh GIMI rate-index finding cut from -0.4 to -0.3, because Q2 showed weak transmission (rates -6%, organic +5%)
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is not a cause) and rule 6 (unverified headline targets): positioning/drawdown finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1
Rule 1 (fact vs reaction; July organic beat earned -0.28%): p_up moved from 52 to 51
Rule 8 (understatement is systematic): abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.2
Rule 6: bar verified against two agreeing estimate sources plus the company guide, and the Q3 organic bar flagged as unsourced
